messages:
incident-bot: Incident created — KV cache pressure spike detected on prod-gpu-pool-3. Alerts: paging rate > 5x baseline, tail latency > 3s. Severity: P1.
jon: I'm on it. seeing lots of evictions + disk spill logs.
maria: rolling up details — happened right after the int8 kernel opt landed in canary at 11:02 UTC.
sai: can you paste the deploy id?
maria: deploy: canary/kernels/2026-03-15-1101 (sha: a1b2c3d). new AWQ->int8 kernel selection change.
devon: customer impact: API 10% error rise, 4 notable customers with latency > 5s, some timeouts.
lucy: support-bot, are any customer-facing incidents open?
support-bot: Not yet, but CS flagged two accounts complaining about slow responses.
jon: quick triage: continuous-batching seems to now include larger per-request KV entries for certain long-context flows. KV entry size distribution shifted right by ~3x.
sai: that would explain spill. The new kernel's kv-layout changed alignment/padding.
jon: attaching logs snippet: ```ERROR kv_cache: spill triggered, item_size=18MB, total_cache=32GB, free=400MB, evict_count=1200/s```
maria: ok immediate mitigation options: 1) revert kernel flag canary -> old selection 2) force smaller batch window (reduce batching_max_tokens) 3) temporarily reduce per-request kv retention TTL 4) throttle large-context requests via routing.
devon: can we do 2+3 quickly? rollback will require a canary rollback and maybe a restart of a subset.
jon: starting with config change: reducing continuous_batch.window_ms from 25 -> 8 on prod-gpu-pool-3. applying now.
infra-bot: config change applied to pool prod-gpu-pool-3: continuous_batch.window_ms=8 by jon at 176999? (ops record).
lucy: noticed immediate dip in average kv item size on a few hosts. tail latency trending down.
sai: but still seeing sporadic large items — need TTL clamp too.
maria: pushing a kludge: set kv.item_max_bytes=6_000_000 (6MB) and kv.drop_on_oversize=true on the pool as emergency.
jon: applied kv.item_max_bytes clamp. monitoring.
support-bot: CS notified affected customers that we're investigating and applying mitigations, ETA 30m.
devon: telemetry: paging rate down from 5x -> 1.3x baseline after these two changes. error rate improving.
sai: good. we should still plan a rollback of the kernel selection from canary to stable for the rest of prod until we root cause.
maria: agree. i'll coordinate rollback with runtime team.
jon: creating a short-lived rate-limit route for >8k token requests to put them on dedicated routing lane (throttle 20rps) so we avoid hitting cache spikes.
lucy: that buys breathing room for rollback.
infra-bot: rollback of canary kernel requested by maria. Estimated impact: 2min per host, rolling.
maria: kickoff rollback now. will monitor.
devon: timeline: 11:17 change batch window -> improvement. 11:23 item_max clamp -> further improvement. rollback started 11:29.
jon: note: we found a config mismatch — the new kernel uses 64-byte kv alignment, old used 32-byte. on long sequences this doubles effective kv footprint.
sai: mitigation checklist: (1) keep kv.item_max_bytes clamp (2) keep reduced batch window (3) finish rollback (4) run a sweep test for alignment bug in memory allocator (5) add unit/regression test for kv footprint in int8 kernel path.
maria: assigning tasks: jon -> monitor prod and validate rollback; sai -> reproduce alignment locally and craft patch; devon -> customer comms + ticketing; lucy -> update runbook; infra -> prepare hotfix canary once patch ready.
jon: rollback finished on all hosts at 11:42. tail latency returned near baseline, paging rate ~1.0x.
support-bot: CS updated customers with mitigation summary and ETA for permanent fix.
devon: two customers still observed transient timeouts during the spike window, logs saved. opening post-incident follow-ups.
sai: early repro shows int8 packing function inserting padding for KV slices when vector length % 64 != 0. patch ready locally.
maria: good. please include microbenchmark numbers and KV footprint delta in PR. we need a targeted patch rather than reverting longer.
jon: follow-up action: revert the alignment change in the kernel codepath and add an allocator test to ensure no explosion for long contexts.
lucy: adding to postmortem: root cause, sequence: kernel selection change -> 64-byte alignment -> KV size increase -> cache spills -> paging -> customer impact. mitigation steps and timelines.
infra-bot: incident transitioned to post-incident review state by maria at 1770000643.
maria: thanks all. we'll schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow 1500 UTC. if anyone has additional logs or repro cases, drop them here. :thumbsup:
jon: uploading heapdump + kv-stat traces to /internal/incidents/1769999999/
devon: I'll follow up with affected customers to ensure they're satisfied with the resolution.
sai: pushing PR now: fix/kv-align-padding-int8. link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4207
maria: great. good job team. closing the live mitigation channel.
